page: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance built on the x86_64 architecture using an Intel Xeon 8269CY CPU clocked at 2.5 GHz. It provides 8 physical cores hyper-threaded into 16 dedicated vCPUs, complemented by a 35 MB L3 cache. The server is allocated 128.0 GB of memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core. This configuration includes no local disk storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and providing a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reflects solid multi-core processing alongside average memory throughput, reaching 76.43 GB/sec uncached read speed and 55.34 GB/sec write speed. Multi-core performance scores across stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark fall into average benchmark tiers. However, single-core processing capabilities are weak, as indicated by lower single-threaded scores in stress-ng and Geekbench. The instance trades raw single-core execution speed for dense RAM capacity relative to vCPU core count.

With its 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.se1.4xlarge is well-suited for memory-bound applications that require high resource density without demanding top-tier single-threaded compute performance. Synthetic tests highlight strong throughput for in-memory operations, including 11.3 million Redis SET operations per second. Recommended workloads include relational databases, in-memory caching tiers, static web serving, software compilation, and light text processing tasks.
